formats.key: Permit(address owner,address spender,uint256 value,uint256 nonce,uint256 deadline)
effects: Once anyone submits the signature to permit() on the 1INCH token (BSC), the allowance the owner gives the spender is set to exactly `value`, replacing the old allowance (ERC20Permit.permit -> _approve(owner, spender, value)).
The signature only works until `deadline` (require(block.timestamp <= deadline)).
Using the signature uses up the owner's current nonce (_nonces[owner].current() then increment). No tokens move until the spender later calls transferFrom.
formats.shown: "Authorize spending of tokens", with the spender address, the maximum amount in 1INCH ("Unlimited" at 2^255 or more), the expiry date and the owner.

findings.title: Permit has no interpolatedIntent, so the one-line summary does not name the amount or the spender.
findings.evidence: descriptor.json display.formats Permit: "intent": "Authorize spending of tokens", no interpolatedIntent. The fields value (tokenAmount) and spender are always visible.
findings.fix: Add interpolatedIntent "Authorize {spender} to spend up to {value} until {deadline}".
